doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Metronome All Stars and Charlie Parker
title: Bob Rowe and the Bleecker Street trio
summary: Prompted by Rowe's name, he recalls a Village trio with bassist Bob Rowe, who later played in New Orleans and hosted a night out.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I’ve got that going for me. Well do you remember a particular—
And Rowe you know, you know, you know—

When we were down in the village, this is before I met any of them guys, maybe I knew Flip, but then we had a trio, a bass, a piano and a guitar. That was like a big hot trio. Carl Senior was the piano player. But Bob Rowe was the bass player. And Bob Rowe — this was down on Bleecker Street and it’s right on the corner, it’s still a bar, and a wild little place.

Yeah. Everybody came in and sit in with this little trio. Bob Rowe had three strings on his bass. It was a three string bass. To this day I’ve never seen one. And he also played a little guitar, he was sort of a Django Reinhardt type. But anyway, well I didn’t mean to get off, but he had your last name. And he wound up to be the principal bass player in the New Orleans Symphony. Me and my wife went out there when I was on the road, and I looked him up. And him and his wife, Dotty, who he was going — she sent him to Juilliard, and she worked as a waitress and let him go to Juilliard, and he became a classical bass player. Very intelligent guy too. But he took us out there and it was a groovy night in New Orleans. First he took us out — first we’d have like some kind of soup and crabs or something, in one place. Then we’d go to another place and have some kind of fish. Then we’d go to another place and have our dessert. In the meantime we were walking all over, it took the whole night, just going to different kinds of places. Pretty groovy.
It sounds like a swinging town.
Yeah. Well that’s where he wound up.
